findings.where: Nav bar lockup (mark + 'MMM INFRA') and the large hero mark, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured. The arches and wordmark are both in the near-black 'cut' (#2A2925). The logo's grey #404040 and the wordmark's blue #0070C0 are gone, and 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' has been dropped. The logo blue appears nowhere in the palette, either as a token or declared logo-only. On granite, the full-colour logo blue falls below 3:1, so this ground needs a one-colour version that Mark does not hold and has not approved.
findings.who_objects: Mark. The brief says the logo stays and must never be redrawn, and he hasn't agreed to a one-colour version. Returning visitors who know the blue MMM Infra wordmark from the current site and his documents would not recognise it.

findings.where: Whole tile, starting with the first screen
findings.fault: There is no photograph of Mark anywhere, not even a labelled stand-in slot. The tile never shows how a portrait or a project photo would sit on the stone ground. The first screen presents a monument (the mark and inscribed capitals), not the man.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff choosing an individual advisor expect to see the real person before they write. Mark's own values ('the man himself', 'the individual is the brand') require it, and the tile cannot answer them.

findings.where: Palette and every place minium is used: the hero name and role, nav interpuncts, the CINZEL specimen, the article title, the texture's 'M', 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED', and the 'Write to Mark' button
findings.fault: Minium is declared as 'headings, the one action', so the action's colour is spent on every heading. Colour no longer singles out the one thing to press. On the first screen, two lines of large red capitals outweigh the small red button. This contradicts the direction's own rule that the one accent 'flows to the action'.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning for what to do, because red means 'heading' as often as it means 'press here'.

findings.where: Article specimen pull quote ('Whichever PPP Law…') against the hero 'Write to Mark' button
findings.fault: The pull quote, which you can't click, takes the button's own shape: a framed panel with dovetail handles. The same tabula ansata shape means 'press me' in the hero and 'read me' in the article.
findings.who_objects: A reader on an article page, who could take the quote for a button or link. It also weakens the button's signature, because that shape no longer means an action.

findings.where: Hero heading 'MARK · M · MOSELEY / INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR'
findings.fault: The name and the role are set at the same size, weight and colour. The longer role line is visibly the heavier of the two, so 'what' outweighs 'who'. Interpuncts also split the middle initial and the phrase 'infrastructure advisor', so the line reads as a list of four separate words rather than a name and a role.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose name is the brand. A visitor reading it quickly gets 'Mark, M, Moseley' and two separate words where they need one person and one role.

findings.where: Article specimen title ('THE WORLD'S BEST PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP LAW') and the type rule 'always in capitals'
findings.fault: Article titles are forced into tracked Cinzel capitals. A five-word title already runs to three lines of capitals at desktop. Mark's real titles, such as 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge', would become dense blocks of capitals that are slow to read.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who adds posts with whatever titles Mark writes. Readers scanning a list of articles also find all-caps titles harder to tell apart.

findings.where: Whole page ground (granite #B8B5AD) and the Texture sample
findings.fault: The page itself is a flat mid-grey with no stone to it. The texture appears only in a boxed diagram that stands in for a photo, and the tile doesn't show where or how that texture meets the page. Across the article and the whole site, the result reads as a dim, drab grey page rather than dressed stone.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for white, a muted colour, blueprint or legal pad, and is shown a grey page whose promised material is missing. Readers of long articles in Read mode get a dull ground with no compensating character.

findings.where: Overall tone: hero, headings, section labels
findings.fault: Red Roman capitals in an inscription layout, with interpuncts throughout, read as a memorial or heritage body. They don't come across as an approachable personal advisor.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for a personal, approachable voice that is not a firm's. Development-bank staff may read the result as themed or pastiche rather than as a working consultant.

findings.where: Hero 'Write to Mark' button and the page as a whole (no footer)
findings.fault: The only contact route is a mailto button. Mark's email address is never shown as text, and there is no footer to carry it.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a work machine where mailto opens nothing or the wrong client. They cannot see or copy the address, so they can't get in touch.

findings.where: Nav bar: 'MMM INFRA' lockup beside the 'PROFILE · ARTICLES · BLOG · CONTACT' links
findings.fault: Two different serif faces in capitals sit side by side at nearly the same size: Gelasio bold for the lockup and tracked Cinzel for the links. They are close enough to look like a mistake rather than a deliberate pairing.
findings.who_objects: Any visitor with an eye for type, and Mark, whose nav bar is the first line of his site.

findings.fault: A button that replays the animation is styled as underlined text, the mark reserved for links. It reads as a link to another page.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects an underlined word to navigate away, and gets the animation replayed instead.
